tldr: Meta had no dedicated AI coding-agent product until Aug 5, 2026, when it introduced Muse Code alongside an updated Muse Spark 1.2, framed explicitly as competition for Claude Code and Codex. CNBC's launch report and three other outlets covered the same framing through Aug 9, with no pricing, availability, or benchmark details disclosed for either product.
whats_new: Coverage of Meta's Aug 5 Muse Code launch continued through Aug 9 with no new pricing, availability, or benchmark specifics disclosed.
why_it_matters: Meta is positioning Muse Code as a Claude Code/Codex rival, but with zero pricing, availability, or benchmark data five days in, there's nothing yet to evaluate against an existing coding-agent stack.

status.detail: Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2 launched Aug 5 with no pricing or availability; Aug 9 coverage repeats the same launch framing without new specifics.

beats.headline: Meta debuts Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2, pitched against Claude Code and Codex
beats.summary: Persistent async background agents is the headline capability; the product is framed explicitly as a Claude Code/Codex rival from day one.

beats.headline: Comparison coverage continues four days later, no new specifics
beats.summary: Aug 9 pickup restates the same launch and comparison framing without pricing, availability, or benchmark updates.

open_questions: Has Meta announced pricing or general availability for Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2?
Do independent benchmarks show how Muse Code's async background agents compare to Claude Code and Codex on real coding tasks?
Is Muse Code available to external developers, or is it limited to Meta's internal/enterprise use?
take_for_builders: Don't switch coding-agent workflows yet — wait for Meta to publish pricing, availability, and independent benchmarks against Claude Code and Codex before evaluating Muse Code.
